issue: Blocked task is entirely uneditable; description and priority cannot be changed
actual: For blocked task "Complete tax filing" (Prerequisite "Review project proposal" incomplete), the edit button (tasks.list.item.4.edit) is disabled=true, so the task form cannot be opened. Clicking the priority badge and the title provides no alternate edit affordance (no task.form appears in snapshot). Result: title and deadline are correctly not editable, but description and priority are also not editable, contrary to the requirement.

evidence: Blocked tasks carry data-semtag-state="blocked", a visible warning row, and complete toggle disabled with class "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50"; clicking tasks.list.item.4.complete timed out because the element is not enabled.

Single incomplete prerequisite: task 4 shows 'Prerequisite "Review project proposal" incomplete'; task c53115bd shows 'Prerequisite "Buy groceries" incomplete'. Multiple: task 7 shows "2 prerequisites incomplete", and its tooltip confirms exactly 2 pending prerequisites.

Hovering tasks.list.item.7.blocked-warning ("2 prerequisites incomplete") opened tooltip: "Dependency Chain / Review project proposal - pending / Complete tax filing - pending", identifying both pending prerequisites.

Dashed SVG connectors (stroke-dasharray="6,4") wrap in hoverable <g class="pointer-events-auto cursor-pointer"> tooltip triggers. Pointer-over on the connector set data-state="delayed-open" and rendered tooltip: "Dependency Chain / Submit final report - pending / Review project proposal - pending / Complete tax filing - pending". (Events dispatched programmatically because the vertical connector has a 0px-wide bounding box.)

Assigned prerequisites "Buy groceries" + "Review project proposal" to task 2 via edit form; saved card shows "2 prerequisites incomplete" and complete/edit disabled (blocked). Earlier single-prerequisite assignment at creation ("Buy groceries" on QA Detailed Task) also retained and displayed.

Edited unblocked task 2: title->"Schedule dentist appointment (edited)", description->"Edited description text", deadline->Sep 15, priority->Low, prerequisites->2 added; all retained after save. Deleted "QA No Deadline Task": removed from list and active count 7->6 ("6 active, 2 completed").

Editing task 1: itself and its direct dependents (2,4,7) were absent from the prerequisite list. After creating chain 1 -> QA Detailed Task -> Buy groceries, editing "Buy groceries" offered only the 2 unrelated completed tasks (5,6); the direct dependent (QA Detailed Task, task 2) and indirect dependents (task 1, 4, 7) were all unavailable, so no cycle can be selected.

Clicked complete on active task "Buy groceries": it disappeared from the active list, counts changed from "6 active, 2 completed" to "5 active, 3 completed", and it appears in the completed view with state completed.

After completion, "Buy groceries" still exists in the completed view (Completed 3: Buy groceries, Reply to client emails, Organize desk) with its data intact and with reopen (toggle-complete), edit and delete controls available.

While "Buy groceries" was incomplete, QA Detailed Task's complete toggle was disabled (blocked). After completing "Buy groceries", QA Detailed Task became active/eligible ("1 prerequisite completed") and its complete toggle worked: counts moved from "5 active, 3 completed" to "4 active, 4 completed".

issue: Reopening a prerequisite leaves its completed dependent simultaneously completed and blocked, in an unrecoverable state
actual: Setup: "QA Detailed Task" (prerequisite "Buy groceries") was completed after its prerequisite was completed. Reopening "Buy groceries" was allowed (counts 4 active/4 completed -> 5 active/3 completed). "QA Detailed Task" stayed in the completed view with data-semtag-state="completed" while also showing the blocked warning 'Prerequisite "Buy groceries" incomplete'. Its complete toggle is enabled=false and its edit button is disabled, so the user cannot reopen or fix it. The system neither prevented the reopen nor returned the dependent to a valid incomplete state.
